'''''Juncus tenageia''''', called the '''sand rush''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Juncus]]'', native to northwestern Africa, many of the Mediterranean islands, warmer parts of southern, central and eastern Europe, and western Asia including Turkey, the Caucasus region, and Kazakhstan.<ref name="443569-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:443569-1 |title=''Juncus tenageia'' Ehrh. ex L.f. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=21 February 2021 }}</ref> It is typically found growing in wet, nutrient-poor rock, sand or clay-based soils, often in clay pits, old brickyards, and on the edges of roads.<ref name="1_of_763_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |last1=Kobierski |first1=Piotr |last2=Ryś |first2=Roman |date=2015 |title=Nowe stanowiska ''Juncus tenageia'' w Borach Dolnośląskich |trans-title=New localities of sand rush ''Juncus tenageia'' in Dolnośląskie Forest (SW Poland) |language=PL |url=http://www.kp.org.pl/pdf/pp/pdf2/PPXXVI_1_kobierski.pdf |journal=Przegląd Przyrodniczy |volume=XXVI |issue=1 |pages=3–10 |access-date=21 February 2021 }}</ref>

==Subtaxa==
The following subspecies are currently accepted:<ref name="443569-1" />
*''Juncus tenageia'' subsp. ''perpusillus'' <small>Fern.-Carv. & F.Navarro</small> – A dwarfed version found in Morocco and the Iberian Peninsula
*''Juncus tenageia'' subsp. ''tenageia''
